target_customer: Career changers and adult learners in Canada paying for coding bootcamps and continuing education
problem: Traditional higher education was slow and costly for people wanting tech careers; Juno offered intensive bootcamps and a pay-what-you-can income share model.
business_model: Tuition for bootcamps and courses, later income share agreements; later shift to training solopreneurs

founders.name: Heather Payne
previous_startups: Ladies Learning Code (not-for-profit team that also started HackerYou)
founders.background_notes: YC page bio names her angel investor and board member at PARC Toronto and Sheertex. Search results say HackerYou was co-founded in 2012 with three others from Ladies Learning Code; names not opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Education delivery with curriculum, instructors and a campus; no hard technology problem.

defensibility.rationale: Bootcamps were easy to copy and several Toronto rivals competed on price and placement outcomes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought Juno. The market fell in 2023 as job placements dropped.

market_need_then: Demand for coding bootcamps in Toronto was high in the mid 2010s, with five of Canada's seven main bootcamps there, and HackerYou was admitted to YC on the strength of a new tuition model.

branding.name_origin: Rebranded from HackerYou to Juno College of Technology, announced June 2019. The company tied the new name to its support for women and non-binary people; the fuller rationale was not seen.
branding.domain_note: Uses junocollege.com; HackerYou used hackeryou.com earlier.

identity.logo: New logo and identity by Studio Function in 2019

branding.brand_signature: Juno is the university of the future tagline

rebrands.why: Tied to support for women and non-binary people and challenging traditional higher education, per press summary

branding.community_and_virality: Roots in Ladies Learning Code community and Course Report reviews from alumni.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong community roots and a design case study, but the Juno name was new and the school stopped admissions in 2023.

pivots.from: Web development bootcamp and continuing education
pivots.why: Dramatic reduction in job placements, per Heather Payne's blog as reported by The Logic

outcome_analysis: HackerYou became Juno College in 2019 and was in YC Summer 2019 with a pay-what-you-can ISA model. In May 2023 it stopped admitting new students to its web development bootcamp and continuing education programs because job placements fell sharply. Course Report now marks the school closed, though the directory lists it Active and it planned a shift to solopreneur training.
notes: Directory status is Active but sources say the bootcamp stopped admitting in 2023 and Course Report marks it closed; exit is recorded as none because no shutdown statement was seen. A $150K seed from YC in August 2019 appears in one aggregator and is unverified. A $4M seed from Hoxton Ventures belongs to a different company called Juno. Competitor list is empty because Toronto bootcamp sources found (Course Report, BetaKit) are undated or later than the batch. The YC page website fetch of the launch page returned 503 and the company site returned 404, so the website is partly dead or moved. Founder education and employers were not found.
